subject: MSA redlines: security exhibit — SOC2 cadence & pen-test access
messages:
From: Justin Park <jpark@medpoint.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security exhibit and inspection cadence - MSA redlines

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal asked me to follow up on the security exhibit language in the MSA and a couple of specific items we need to understand before we can sign the order form:

1) SOC 2: are you committing to an annual SOC 2 Type II report? Can we request a copy and what is your expected turnaround if a customer asks?
2) Pen test: what language do you propose for pen-test notice and scope? Do you provide a customer-facing statement that Redwood performs third-party penetration testing on an annual cadence?
3) Inspection / evidence access: our security team needs clarity on what "audit rights" mean in practice — sampling windows, staging access, ability to request specific artifact sets (logs, configs), and redaction policy for sensitive fields.
4) Evidence cadence: we'd like to align on a quarterly/rolling evidence cadence rather than ad-hoc requests. Is that acceptable?

I've attached our questionnaire (MedPoint_SecurityQ_2026.pdf) that shows the specific artifacts they're asking for. Can you send proposed redline language for the security exhibit and order form? If useful we can schedule a short call with procurement + legal.

Thanks,
Justin Park
IT Procurement | MedPoint Health
justin.park@medpoint.com
Attachment: MedPoint_SecurityQ_2026.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Justin Park <jpark@medpoint.com>
Cc: Monique Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security exhibit and inspection cadence - MSA redlines

Justin — thanks for the questionnaire and clear asks. I can absolutely take point. We can provide the standard SOC 2 Type II report annually to customers under an NDA; turnaround for an on-request copy is typically 2-3 business days via our secure portal.

Regarding pen tests: Redwood runs an annual third-party penetration test and maintains a summary report we provide to customers; detailed exploit data is retained internally but we can provide a customer-facing executive summary and remediation status. For inspection rights and evidence cadence, we generally propose a bounded inspection window, sampling approach, and redaction rights for PII and customer data.

I'll loop in Legal and Security to draft redline language and propose an evidence cadence that matches your quarterly preference. Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Friday 12/4 to walk MedPoint Legal & Procurement through the draft?

Action items: 
- I'll circulate proposed redline for the security exhibit + short summary of concessions (Tessa).
- Legal will review pen-test/inspection carveouts and backstop language (Monique + Karthik).
- We'll include a sample evidence schedule for a quarterly rolling window.

If that works, send one or two time slots for Friday.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monique Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: MedPoint - security exhibit redline positions and ops ask

Team — looping you in to coordinate legal redlines and product/security positions for MedPoint (deal MP-2026-189). Justin sent their questionnaire (attached). Key negotiation points I want us aligned on before we share anything externally: 

1) SOC 2 delivery: we can commit to providing the SOC 2 Type II report annually under NDA. External ask: customers want a copy on request. Proposed position: provide a verified report via secure portal within 3 business days after request, subject to NDA.

2) Pen test language: they ask for an annual pen test and visibility. Proposed position: Redwood performs an annual third-party penetration test; we will share an executive summary with remediation status and allow customers to request a controlled review of findings summary. No full raw exploit details or attacker PII will be shared. If customer requests additional forensic-level data, we require a legal review and a scoped agreement.

3) Inspection / audit rights: customer wants broad "inspection rights". Proposed position: a bounded inspection window (up to 5 business days on staging with pre-approved engineers), sampling of artifacts limited to a pre-agreed artifact matrix (logs, config summaries, vulnerability scan exports, SOC 2 control mappings), and redaction rights for sensitive platform telemetry. We should explicitly call out operational carveouts (no live production access, no on-demand memory dumps, no access to other tenant data).

4) Evidence cadence: MedPoint prefers a quarterly cadence. Proposed compromise: offer a quarterly rolling evidence pack (selected artifacts and control attestations) plus 1 ad-hoc request per 12 months (subject to scheduling and NDAs). Capture a mechanism for prioritized artifact lists to be submitted 10 business days prior to any window.

5) Escalation and remediation: include an SLA for remediation updates (30/60/90 day buckets) and a single point of contact on our side (security liaison).

6) KMS/HSM and key controls: confirm we support customer-managed keys for private deployment; for hosted accounts provide details of KMS integrations and redaction policy.

Please review the attached proposed-security-exhibit-redline-v1.docx and add redlined edits by EOD Thursday. Laura — can you confirm the operational feasibility for the 5 business day staging window and the artifact matrix? Karthik/Monique — please sanity-check legal positions on the inspection carveouts and the one ad-hoc request allowance.

Thanks — once we have internal agreement I'll push back to Justin with tracked changes and a short reconciliation table.

Tessa
Attachment: proposed-security-exhibit-redline-v1.docx (docx, 48KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Security exhibit and inspection cadence - MSA redlines

Hi Justin / MedPoint team — thanks for the questionnaire and for the time last Friday. Attached is our proposed redline (proposed-security-exhibit-redline-v1.docx) and a short reconciliation summary (Redlines_Summary_20261206.xlsx) that maps each of your asks to our position. High-level summary below: 

- SOC 2: we will provide the annual SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and can deliver a copy via our secure portal within 3 business days of request.
- Pen test: Redwood conducts an annual third-party penetration test. We will provide customers with an executive summary and remediation status. Full raw exploit data is not shared; requests for deeper forensic material will require a scoped legal agreement.
- Inspection / evidence access: proposed bounded staging window (up to 5 business days) and an artifact matrix that limits requests to specific categories (logs, config summaries, vulnerability scans, control mappings). No production-level access; no cross-tenant data.
- Evidence cadence: we propose a quarterly rolling evidence package plus one ad-hoc request per 12-month period (requests to be submitted at least 10 business days before a window).

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached redline and reconciliation table. 
2) If the redline is acceptable, we will prepare an amendment to the Order Form (DocuSign link below) for signatures. If you need further edits, please mark them in the docx and return.
